RaMP returned Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) as the top two hits, both at FDR 4.25×10⁻¹¹ with four shared driver metabolites: sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactinol (C01235), and glycerol (C00116). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) first with p=3.25×10⁻⁷, hitting the same four metabolites. Mummichog's empirical network ranked galactose metabolism fourth (p=8.4×10⁻⁵) and starch-and-sucrose metabolism third, with fructose 1-phosphate (C01094) and D-glucose (C00221) contributing network-network coverage. Deoxycytidine (C00881) appeared only in the broad Reactome metabolism and WikiPathways biochemical-pathways hits, suggesting peripheral involvement. The galactose-metabolism convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and network (mummichog) paradigms is robust: four input metabolites map directly to the pathway in two independent databases, with fold-enrichment >1000 in RaMP. Galactinol is the pathway-specific sentinel (galactose donor to myo-inositol via raffinose-family biosynthesis), while sucrose and glycerol bridge to broader hexose and glycerolipid metabolism.
